body:
## Summary

Since v1.16.0, Vite SSR builds (Nitro, TanStack Start) produce broken bundles when any code in the SSR bundle transitively imports a workflow module. The bundle ends up with two classes of unresolvable imports:

1. **Bare deep imports** like `import * as errors from '@temporalio/common/lib/errors'` — Node's ESM resolver rejects these (no `.js` extension, package has no `exports` field).
2. **Absolute local file-system paths** like `import * as cancellationScope from '/Users/me/proj/node_modules/.pnpm/@temporalio+workflow@1.17.2/node_modules/@temporalio/workflow/lib/cancellation-scope'` — won't resolve anywhere except the original build machine.

At runtime the server crashes with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/@temporalio/common/lib/errors' imported from .../router-XYZ.mjs
Did you mean to import "@temporalio/common/lib/errors.js"?
```

## Repro setup

- Vite ^7.2, TanStack Start ^1.132, `@tanstack/nitro-v2-vite-plugin` (Nitro preset `node-server`)
- pnpm workspace
- Web app server-side code imports a workflow barrel from a workspace package, e.g.:
  ```ts
  // packages/web/src/temporal/index.ts
  import { createUploadRecordWorkflow, uploadDoneSignal, … } from '@letschurch/temporal/workflows/background';
  ```
- The workspace package re-exports workflow functions and signal/query definitions from individual workflow files, each of which `import { proxyActivities } from '@temporalio/workflow'` etc.
- The workspace package is in Vite's `ssr.external` list, but Vite inlines workspace packages anyway.

## Bisect

Only the `@temporalio/*` catalog versions changed between builds. Everything else identical.

| @temporalio/* | router chunk: total imports | router chunk: absolute-path imports | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.13.2 | 2 (named, clean) | 0 | ✅ |
| 1.14.0 | 2 (named, clean) | 0 | ✅ |
| 1.15.0 | 2 (named, clean) | 0 | ✅ |
| **1.16.0** | **35** | **23** | ❌ |
| 1.17.2 | 36 | 24 | ❌ |

The 1.16 release notes call out a Nexus API restructuring (#1993, #1979, #1998 — `NexusClient → NexusServiceClient`, interceptor I/O type renames, `executeStartOperation`/`executeCancelOperation`). I suspect one of those PRs added a re-export shape that interacts badly with Rollup/Vite's tree-shaking when the package is marked external — Vite/Rollup decides to "see through" the externalized package's barrel and emit direct deep-path imports to the underlying CJS files instead of treating the package as opaque.

## Concrete bundle diffs

Working bundle (1.15.0):

```js
import { defineSignal, proxyActivities, setHandler, condition, startChild, ParentClosePolicy, defineQuery, executeChild, workflowInfo, continueAsNew, sleep as sleep$1, isCancellation, CancellationScope } from '@temporalio/workflow';
import { Client, Connection } from '@temporalio/client';
```

Broken bundle (1.16.0 and later):

```js
import * as common$1 from '@temporalio/common';
import * as errors$2 from '@temporalio/common/lib/errors';
import * as workflowHandle from '@temporalio/common/lib/workflow-handle';
import * as cancellationScope from '/Users/me/.../node_modules/.pnpm/@temporalio+workflow@1.17.2/node_modules/@temporalio/workflow/lib/cancellation-scope';
import * as asyncCompletionClient from '/Users/me/.../node_modules/.pnpm/@temporalio+client@1.17.2/node_modules/@temporalio/client/lib/async-completion-client';
// ... 30+ more
```

## Workarounds tried (none worked)

- `ssr.noExternal: ['@temporalio/common', '@temporalio/workflow']` → more absolute paths, including into `@temporalio/client` internals.
- `nitroV2Plugin({ externals: { external: [...] } })` → no effect; the broken imports come from Vite's SSR phase, not Nitro's trace.
- Pinning back to 1.15.0 → works, but loses 1.16+ features (Nexus changes).

The only durable client-side workaround is to never have a workflow module in the SSR bundle's import graph — refactor host code to use string workflow names and type-only imports for typing.

## Related

- #2079 — Use package.json `exports` to define cross-package entry points (would prevent class-1 bare deep imports)
- #1280 — Bundle using Vite (generic feature request)
- #1615 — Cannot use Temporal with NextJS 15 because workflowTypes come from function names (same family of bundler/SDK friction, different mechanism)

comments.body: I am also hitting this roadblock since version 1.16 within a Nuxt project.

In the short term, we expect to tackle #2079 which should help.

In the meantime your workaround of avoiding importing the workflow code entirely is all we can offer.

title: [Bug] Vite SSR emits broken imports for workflow modules starting in 1.16.0
